answers.core: This behavior seems much more intuitive to what people use the "Reparent to New Node" feature for than creating a seemingly unrelated node. And as stated before, each time someone would run into this issue, it would probably only cost about a minute or two to solve, but level designers would run into this situation quite a few times throughout the creation of a game.
answers.workaround: This can be worked around with a plugin, but the time lost trying to fix it each time is so small that I don't believe most users would go out of their way to find a plugin to solve this.

title: New node created from "Reparent to New Node" positioned relative to the child nodes, not the origin
